description.narrative: Insatsens övergripande mål är att öka tillgången till juridisk rådvigning för marginaliserade grupper i Nordmakedonien

Kvinna till Kvinna har ansökt om finansiering av egeninsats om 798 413 SEK för EU-projektet "Access to justice for marginalized communities" för perioden 2020-2022. Projektet implementeras av Kvinna till Kvinna partnerorganisation Coalition Sexual and Health rights of Marginalized Communities (MARGINS) i samarbete med tre lokala partners i Nordmakedonien.
Insatsens övergripande mål är att öka tillgången till juridisk rådgivning för marginaliserade grupper i Nordmakedonien. Insatsen syftar även till att:
1. Öka medvetenheten, engagemanget och kapaciteten bland människor som lever i fattigdom att arbeta för demokrati och utkräva sina mänskliga rättigheter.
2. Öka möjligheterna för det civila samhället att främja en gynnsam miljö.
Insatsen har en total budget på 212 555 EUR, vilket motsvarar cirka 2 338 105 SEK. Av detta har Kvinna till Kvinna beviljats 140 000 EUR från EU-kommissionen och 798 413 SEK från Sida. Sidas bidrag till egeninsatsen utgör 35,6 % av det totala beloppet.

Kvinna till Kvinna has applied to Sida for co-funding of 798 413 SEK to carry out the EU project "Access to justice for marginalized communities" during the period 2020-2022. The project is implemented by Kvinna till Kvinna's partner organization Coalition Sexual and Health rights of Marginalized Communities (MARGINS) in cooperation with three local partners in Nort Macedonia.
The project's overall objective is to increase legal access for margnialized groups in North Macedonia. The project also aims to contribute to:
1. Greater awareness, engagement and capacity among people living in poverty, enabling them to work for democracy and to organise in order to assert their human rights.
2. Increased opportunities for civil society to promote an enabling environment.
The contribution's total budget is 212 555 EUR, which corresponds to approximately 2 338 105 SEK. The requested support from Sida is 798 413 SEK, which corresponds to 35,6 % of the total budget.

- "During the 24-month implementation period, significant progress was made towards these two objectives, also contributing to the fulfilment of the goals of the Swedish Government's Strategy for Support Through Swedish Organizations in Civil Society 2016-2022. In line with the priorities set out in the strategy, a key target during the project has been improving the capacities of CSOs to work within the broader human rights framework. Numerous sub-grantee activities were implemented during the reporting period including registering the local organisations as legal aid providers with the Ministry of Justice; applying innovative approaches with tangible impact on beneficiaries and marginalised communities; providing comprehensive package of services combining legal aid with psychosocial support; promoting services, raising awareness and empowering marginalised communities to report right violations; outreach and visibility including a public campaign aimed at creating an enabling environment for protection of the rights of the marginalized communities; and advocacy toward relevant duty-bearers and stakeholders at local and national level".
- "Furthermore, the project has contributed specifically to the second point of the first goal of the strategy, Greater awareness, engagement and capacity among people living in poverty, enabling them to work for democracy and to organise in order to assert their human rights. During the implementation period, CSOs and members of marginalised communities were strengthened in documenting cases of human right violations. Specifically, 35 representatives from marginalised communities were trained to document cases on human rights violations, and 19 members of marginalised communities have since actively documented cases of human rights violations. This increased knowledge and subsequent practice impacts the degree to which marginalised people organise to assert their human rights. In total, 168 cases of rights violations were documented, exceeding the identified target of 150 cases".
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
